chapter: Youth, Storyville and the bands he heard
title: Personnel and instrumentation of the Superior band
summary: Players in Billy Moreira's Superior band, and use of guitars, banjos, pianos, violins and string bass in early small bands.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Oh man, I don't know. Well he used to use Peter Boccage, Richard Payne, Bonk, either Buddy or Yannick, I can't remember which. It must have been Buddy. I think Buddy was a better reader than Yannick.

Yeah, well I don't know, but Buddy and Yannick, poor for some one player. Yeah. Yeah. And Walter Brundy, I think you used. Walter Brundy was a drummer. Yeah. He worked with Roebeshaw for a long, long time. All the time I knew him used to work with John Roebeshaw.
Billy had the, Billy Moreira had the Superior. Yeah. Yeah, that's right.
Usually he had small bands, I see. Yeah. Did they use guitars or banjos in those bands? Did they use guitars?

They used to use guitars, and then they went, they changed to six string banjos, and some of them went back to guitars. They never had no pianos? No, well a few had pianos. A few of them had. It was kind of a hard matter to get these pianos on a job, see, unless there was one there already. Did they use violins in those bands? They used violins. Did the Man of Correa's band have a violin? No, they didn't have no violin in his band. No. They had a clarinet trombone, for his bow trombone, they did. And him showed the trumpet and the drums. About six or so.
They used string bass, I guess. Yeah, string bass.
